clue.text: Philosopher showing aptitude, performer going over the top?

parts.note: a bent is a natural talent or aptitude
a ham is an actor who overacts

explanation.surface: A thinker who shows real talent but plays to the gallery like a hammy actor.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeremy Bentham was the English philosopher who founded utilitarianism.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeremy Bentham is a famous English utilitarian thinker, so an example of the category.

clue.text: Happen to be facing revolutionary change

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the word for change is read backwards

parts.note: to edit is to change a text

explanation.surface: A call to be ready for radical change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facing' just places one piece beside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To betide is to befall or happen to someone, as in woe betide you.

clue.text: Youngest sheep in Australian territory

indicators.note: in places the sheep inside the territory

parts.note: NT is the Northern Territory of Australia
ewes are female sheep

explanation.surface: The youngest lambs are found in an Australian outback territory.
explanation.definitionFit: The most recent arrival is the latest, the most recently born.

clue.text: Flowering plant exciting holier poet

indicators.note: exciting is taken as stirring up, so the letters are stirred

explanation.surface: A blossom thrills a devout poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A heliotrope is a garden shrub with fragrant purple blooms.

clue.text: What is noted to be the 'food of love'?

definitions.text: What is noted to be the 'food of love'?

parts.words: What is noted to be the 'food of love'?
parts.note: 'noted' means both well known and written in notes

explanation.surface: A quiz question asking what is famously called the food of love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noted' means both famous and set down in musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Orsino calls melody and song the food of love.

clue.text: Distant artist needing energy, in disordered state

parts.note: far means distant
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: A remote painter who lacks drive is in a bit of a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrago is a confused jumble or medley, a muddled mixture of things.

clue.text: Pleasant influence of guy in European country

indicators.note: in places the teasing word inside the country

parts.note: France is a country in Europe
to guy someone is to mock them, as is to rag them

explanation.surface: A man in France has a pleasing effect on people.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet scent is an agreeable effect on the senses, a perfume.

clue.text: Bird to perceive the sound of river rising

indicators.note: in a down clue rising sends the river letter up to the top

parts.note: to hear is to perceive the sound of something

explanation.surface: Listening for a bird near a river in flood.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhea is a large flightless South American bird like an ostrich.

clue.text: Like a fog around end of October creating panic

indicators.note: around puts the two words round the end letter of October

parts.note: a la means in the manner of, like
a mist is a light fog

indicators.note: end of signals the last letter of October is taken

explanation.surface: A late October fog descends and causes alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarmist spreads needless fear, so the adjective describes something stirring up worry.

clue.text: Set aside across the street, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear signals that the words are spoken and give a soundalike

parts.note: over the road means across the street

explanation.surface: A puzzle about something put aside on the other side of the road.
explanation.definitionFit: To override a decision is to set it aside or overrule it.

clue.text: Garden tool not right — it should be drier

indicators.note: not tells us the following letter is left out of the tool

parts.note: a trowel is a small hand tool for gardening

explanation.surface: A gardener complains that a tool missing something should at least dry off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drier' is a thing that dries, not the comparative of dry.
explanation.definitionFit: A towel is a cloth used for drying, so it is literally a drying thing.

clue.text: Unexciting partner in an impasse

parts.note: stale means flat or unexciting
a mate is a partner or companion

explanation.surface: A dull spouse in a relationship that has stopped going anywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock in which neither side can progress; originally a chess position with no legal move.

clue.text: Band's ending — is gig put off?

indicators.note: ending signals the last letter of the band word is taken

parts.note: a gig is a concert

explanation.surface: A band breaks up and wonders whether its show has been postponed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put off' looks like 'postponed' but means unsettle.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsettle or fluster someone is to put them off, the same sense as disturb.

clue.text: Ruler starts to expect miracles immediately, right?

indicators.note: starts to signals the opening letters of the next four words are taken

explanation.surface: A sceptic asks whether a leader should be expected to perform wonders on demand.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a Muslim prince or commander, a kind of monarch.

clue.text: Idiots obstruct leaders

parts.note: block means obstruct
heads are leaders or chiefs

explanation.surface: Fools getting in the way of their bosses.
explanation.definitionFit: Blockheads are stupid people, dolts and fools.

clue.text: Claim dire sin somehow should be made illegal

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are put together in some other way

explanation.surface: A moralist argues that a terrible sin ought to be outlawed.
explanation.definitionFit: To criminalise something is to turn it into an offence by law.

clue.text: Meal drama — terrible breakfast food?

indicators.note: terrible suggests the letters are in a terrible mess

explanation.surface: A dramatic scene at the table over a dreadful breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Orange preserve spread on toast is a classic British morning spread.

clue.text: Give sign of approval to maiden perhaps seen as idle

parts.note: to tick is to mark something as approved
a maiden is a cricket over in which no runs are scored

explanation.surface: Approving a young woman who seems to be lazing about.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a maiden over is one where no runs are scored.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine that is idling runs slowly without moving the vehicle.

clue.text: Ordained theologian goes round estate with trendy curate finally

indicators.note: goes round puts the theologian's letters on either side

parts.note: DD is a Doctor of Divinity
EST is an abbreviation for estate
in means fashionable

indicators.note: finally signals the last letter of curate is taken

explanation.surface: A divinity scholar tours an estate with a fashionable young cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordained here means decreed by fate, preordained, so fated in advance.

clue.text: Green type shows this problem

parts.note: a green type is a novice, whose difficulty is a lack of practice; 'Green' might suggest an environmentalist

explanation.surface: An environmentalist turns out to be the source of some trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' tempts towards ecology, but here it means raw and untried.
explanation.definitionFit: A green novice's shortcoming is lack of practice or knowledge, which is exactly this noun.

clue.text: Peril created by fellows leading a church

indicators.note: leading puts the fellows in front of the rest

parts.note: men are fellows
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Danger caused by men who run a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A menace is a threat or danger, the same sense as hazard.

clue.text: People dealing with needles in channels

definitions.meaning: those who sew, working with needle and thread
drains or underground conduits for waste

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both people who stitch and underground drains, pronounced differently.

clue.text: Christopher, husband in social group

parts.note: Kit is a short form of the name Christopher

explanation.surface: A man called Christopher and his husband move in a particular circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Kith are one's friends and acquaintances, as in the phrase kith and kin.

clue.text: Cheddar rather than brie? Bad luck!

definitions.meaning: cheddar is a firm cheese while brie is soft
an informal British exclamation of mock sympathy meaning tough luck

explanation.surface: Someone offered cheddar when they wanted brie is told it is just too bad.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a literal firm dairy product and British slang for tough luck.

clue.text: Acts to produce legal documents

definitions.meaning: a deed is a signed legal document, such as one for property

explanation.surface: Actions that result in paperwork.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both actions done and formal property contracts.

clue.text: One lacking intelligence brought up in part of France

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
dim means stupid

explanation.surface: A slow-witted person raised in a region of France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Midi is the south of France, a region.

clue.text: A vile tent — foul air

indicators.note: foul suggests the letters are fouled up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A horrid tent with stale air inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foul air' reads as a noun phrase, but 'air' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To air a room is to let fresh breeze through it, the same action as freshen.

clue.text: Star must get hold of office assistant quickly

indicators.note: the star word is to grasp the assistant, so one goes round the other

parts.note: an ace is a star performer
PA is a personal assistant

explanation.surface: A top employee is told to grab a secretary in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Apace is an old-fashioned adverb for at speed or swiftly.

clue.text: King, a Northumbrian one, first to enjoy alcoholic drink

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king (rex)
Edwin was a seventh-century King of Northumbria

indicators.note: first to signals the opening letter of enjoy is taken

explanation.surface: An old Northumbrian monarch is the first to enjoy a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Northumbria was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret or merlot, fermented from dark grapes, is a kind of alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Resists abnormally religious women

indicators.note: abnormally means the letters are set out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Someone resists in an odd way, perhaps a group of nuns.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuns are addressed as Sister, so a convent's members are these women.
